summary: Postinstall auto-executes opaque bundled Windows PE with packer/stealer indicators
details: On Windows, this package's postinstall script (postinstall.js) detaches and launches a bundled 34 MB executable at assets/Helper.exe with no hash or signature verification, triggered automatically by `npm install`. The launch uses spawn(exe, [], { detached: true, stdio: "ignore" }) with child.unref(), gated on process.platform === "win32", and is wired via package.json "postinstall": "node./postinstall.js". The shipped PE (sha256 e5a585e03e1725d5030fd4854805933d53aa86cfbbb0b3808dffcc63782ddf38) imports AES/BCrypt decryption routines (BCryptDecrypt, BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey), Authenticode/Catalog APIs (WinVerifyTrust, CryptCATAdminAcquireContext2), VirtualProtect for runtime memory-protection changes, process/file manipulation (CreateProcessA, CopyFile, CreateDirectory, DeleteFile), environment reads for USERDOMAIN/USERNAME/APPDATA, shell-window enumeration (EnumWindows, GetShellWindow), a base64 alphabet constant, and large high-entropy string blocks — the fingerprint of a packed native loader rather than the trivial "opens on install" behavior stated in the README. The package has no legitimate functional purpose that would justify auto-executing an unidentified native binary on every Windows installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
